A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Concept2Concept research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and added or removed material.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original concept-frequency and co-occurrence analyses, bias-probing replications, and audits of Pick-a-Pic and StableImageNet, with supporting appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical analyses and adds cross-model comparisons and a ten-image ChatGPT-interface audit in Appendices A.7–A.8.

M1.justification: The prompt sampling, image generation, concept detection/localization, frequency, stability, and co-occurrence procedures remain unchanged. The added generators are auditing targets; the expanded negative-prompting explanation does not establish a new algorithm or intervention.

E1.justification: Both versions cover age/action prompts, professions, disabilities, Pick-a-Pic, and StableImageNet. The new model comparisons reuse retained prompt types. Removing one illustrative class gallery does not establish that the class was excluded from the StableImageNet audit.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the StableBias and TBYB comparisons. OpenBias is added only to related work. Lumina, SD3 Medium, and ChatGPT are additional generators being audited, rather than competing auditing methods evaluated against Concept2Concept.

E3.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a fixed-prompt comparison across Lumina Next SFT, SD 2.1, and SD3 Medium for three disability prompts and one jogging prompt. A.8 adds a ten-image ChatGPT-interface protocol. These substantially extend the evaluation design, while the original settings tables remain essentially unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine how concept representations vary across generators and demonstrate auditing of a closed-source model (A.7–A.8). They add concept distributions and example images for these questions. Conversely, v1's Figure 22, the StableImageNet class 680 ('nipple') misalignment gallery, is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random samples of 1,000 Pick-a-Pic entries and confidence intervals for the corresponding concept detections. v2 introduces no new seed reporting, repeated-run procedure, confidence-interval practice, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds cross-model concept frequencies and generated-image examples in Figures 12–19, plus the ChatGPT results in Figures 20–21, where wheelchair detection frequency is 1.0 across ten images. It removes v1's class 680 gallery. Table 1 and the retained original plots are unchanged; the additions concern new experimental conditions.

T1.justification: Section 3 changes the detector-distribution assumption: v1 allows stochastic concept extraction and identifies deterministic extraction as a special case, whereas v2 explicitly assumes deterministic extraction with a delta distribution. Equations 1–6 remain unchanged, and no new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: interpretable concept-based auditing, the Pick-a-Pic and StableImageNet findings, and an open-source interactive tool. The additional experiments support the existing framework claim without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds a mechanism explanation connecting negative prompting to replacement of unconditional text in classifier-free guidance. v2 also explicitly discusses applicability to closed-source models presumed to be safety-tuned. The original result interpretations, ethics discussion, and principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a demo link, expands Jupyter/Colab usage information, and explains the negative-conditioning implementation. It identifies the additional audited models and the ten-image closed-source setup, but provides limited generation settings for the new cross-model comparisons. Original hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands the methodological positioning: it adds OpenBias and arguments about VQA question constraints and LLM overhead, and specifies claimed localization and scalability limitations of TBYB and CUPID. Section 4.2 newly presents earlier auditors as special cases of Concept2Concept. Lumina and SD3 references are also added.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits and rewrites selected passages, subdivides related work, adds an experimental-setup overview, retitles several sections, and expands the tool description. The overall seven-section narrative and most original explanations are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography, headings, table wrapping, and figure placement throughout. It adds grouped model-comparison plots and image strips plus a closed-source chart/gallery in Figures 12–21, removes v1's Figure 22, and relocates retained appendix material. The original main figures and interface screenshots are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: The new audits in A.7–A.8 provide useful additional evidence for applicability across generators, while the negative-prompting explanation and demo link improve usability. The main findings remain intact despite removal of one illustrative StableImageNet gallery. These gains are limited by sparse settings for the new comparisons and a new inconsistency: the experimental overview says Application 1 uses SD 2.1, whereas Table 2 still specifies SDXL-Lightning.
